title: MLX grain uses a normal approximation and violates the repository GPU parity contract
evidence: The MLX branch documents and implements a normal approximation for Binomial(seeds,p) at grain.py:141-159. A fixed-seed smoke probe on the current tree compared CPU apply_grain_to_density against MLX apply_grain_to_density for a 16x16x3 density field and printed max_abs=0.5796337127685547, allclose_1e-6=False, while both arrays were float32. Existing tests only assert deterministic MLX output and loose mean plausibility.
impact: Users selecting MLX with grain enabled can get materially different grain structure from the CPU reference. This contradicts the project instruction that GPU output must be numerically identical or within float32 epsilon to CPU/NumPy unless explicitly falling back.
trigger: compute_backend='mlx' or backend-resident MLX runtime with grain enabled and method='poisson_binomial'.
recommendation: Either implement an exact backend binomial/poisson-binomial path matching the CPU algorithm and seed contract, or explicitly route grain to CPU when exact parity cannot be provided. Add a fixed-seed CPU-vs-MLX parity test using np.allclose(..., atol=1e-6).
validation: Run a new test that compares CPU and MLX grain on identical density, seed, pixel_size_um, grain_blur and asserts max_abs <= 1e-6; also assert backend fallback behavior if exact GPU parity is not supported.

title: MLX soft_update can use stale backend print illuminant tables after enlarger filter changes
evidence: PrintingStage precomputes _backend_print_illuminant once at construction from enlarger filters (printing.py:50-73). SimulationPipeline.soft_update mutates c_filter_neutral, m_filter_neutral and y_filter_neutral (pipeline.py:411-430) but does not refresh the cached backend table. A current-tree probe using MLX float32, spatial/stochastic disabled, and c_filter_neutral=80.0 printed soft_rebuilt_max_abs=0.5277431011199951 between soft-updated and freshly rebuilt pipelines.
impact: Interactive GUI or API soft updates can show/export colors that do not correspond to the current filter controls on MLX, with large visible color differences.
trigger: MLX/GPU pipeline constructed once, then Simulator.soft_update(c_filter_neutral=... or m/y_filter_neutral=...) followed by process().
recommendation: Invalidate or recompute PrintingStage backend spectral tables whenever enlarger filter, illuminant, preflash, or any input to enlarger_filtered_illuminant changes. Add a soft-update-vs-rebuild parity test for CPU and MLX.
validation: Repeat the smoke with MLX and assert soft-updated output matches a freshly rebuilt MLX pipeline and CPU reference within the existing GPU tolerance.

title: RouteMaster HDR accepts an output_diffuse_white control but only records it in diagnostics
evidence: HDRProjectionConfig validates output_diffuse_white at projection.py:22 and 44-45, but _build_result builds hdr_rgb from chroma*hdr_y, preserves SDR for paper below scene anchor, computes headroom/gain map, and only writes output_diffuse_white into diagnostics at projection.py:203-229. rg found no production use outside validation and tests that assert the diagnostic value.
impact: The GUI/user-visible diffuse white target can appear to control HDR output brightness while not affecting the actual HDR rendition or gain-map math. This is a unit/semantic mismatch in a critical HDR export path.
trigger: Explicit HDR HEIC export using a non-default hdr_diffuse_white_target/output_diffuse_white value.
recommendation: Either apply output_diffuse_white to the HDR projection/gain-map luminance contract with tests proving the target, or rename/remove the control so it is not presented as an output target. Keep scene anchor and output target as separate concepts.
validation: Add a projection test where output_diffuse_white differs from diffuse_white_scene_anchor and assert the HDR diffuse-white output and gain map metadata change as specified.

title: Mid-pipeline topology injection can skip preprocess side effects and crash active spatial DIR couplers
evidence: _process_topology seeds only the requested inject tap and calls run_topology (pipeline.py:228-239). Spatial DIR couplers divide diffusion_size_um by pixel_size_um at couplers.py:173-175. A current-tree smoke with default digested params and process(log_e, inject=Tap.LOG_E_FILM, collect=Tap.CMY_FILM) failed with TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for /: 'float' and 'NoneType'.
impact: A public-looking runtime tap API crashes for default parameters when injected after preprocess, which makes LUT/debug/topology tooling fragile and undocumented.
trigger: SimulationPipeline.process(..., inject='log_e_film', collect='cmy_film') or equivalent taps while spatial effects remain enabled.
recommendation: Initialize pixel_size_um from explicit image geometry before downstream stages, require callers to provide it, or reject such injections unless spatial effects are disabled. Add real pipeline injection tests, not only standalone topology dispatcher tests.
validation: Add tests for default params and debug.lut_mode covering inject/collect combinations through real SimulationPipeline.

title: RouteMaster HEIC metadata is passed through the stack and then discarded; GUI metadata copy is a no-op for HEIC
evidence: export_hdr_heic_from_simulator passes metadata={'hdr_mode': mode, 'route_kind': master.route_kind} at routemaster_export.py:80-88. save_hdr_photo_heic_from_pair accepts metadata and immediately del metadata at hdr_photo.py:350-368. After export, GUI save_output_layer tries write_image_metadata, but write_image_metadata returns immediately for HEIC/HEIF at io.py:117-118, so controller.py:460-485 can report success without any copied metadata.
impact: HEIC exports can lose route/source metadata and copied camera metadata while the GUI gives no user-visible warning. This weakens provenance and downstream HDR debugging.
trigger: GUI or API RouteMaster HEIC/HEIF export with source metadata or expected route metadata.
recommendation: Remove the misleading metadata parameter or encode the metadata into XMP/Exif/HEIF boxes through the actual CoreImage/ImageIO path. Make GUI status distinguish unsupported HEIC metadata copying from success.
validation: Export a small HEIC with metadata, then read it back with ImageIO/exiftool/sips/mdls and assert required route/source tags are present or that the UI reports metadata unsupported.

title: Gain-map loaders silently degrade to partial results and HEIF metadata extraction is unimplemented
evidence: _load_gain_map_jpeg catches gain-map decode failures with except Exception: pass at gain_map_io.py:361-365. _load_gain_map_heif always returns metadata=None with a comment that ISOBMFF parsing would be needed at gain_map_io.py:509-512. Static search shows older audit docs already flagged HEIF metadata extraction as deferred.
impact: Corrupt or incompatible gain-map files can look like successful base-image loads, and HEIF metadata round-trips cannot prove headroom/gain-map semantics.
trigger: load_gain_map() on JPEG with broken MPF gain-map payload or HEIF gain-map files where metadata is required.
recommendation: Return explicit warnings/errors for failed gain-map decode and implement or clearly expose HEIF ISO 21496 metadata parsing status. Tests should fail when metadata is expected but absent.
validation: Add corrupted MPF and HEIF fixtures; assert a structured error or warning rather than metadata=None success.

title: GUI display transform materializes full frames and quantizes to uint8 before display-profile conversion
evidence: prepare_output_display_image calls np.asarray(image_data)[..., :3] for the full source at controller_runtime.py:391-393, always constructs an 8-bit preview at 394-396, and apply_display_transform converts source data to uint8 before ImageCms profileToProfile at 342-355. HDR/linear branches also clip to [0,1] before uint8 conversion at 316 and 329.
impact: Large MLX/backend-resident previews incur full-frame CPU materialization and copies. Wide-gamut/HDR preview fidelity is limited to 8-bit SDR before display transform, which can mask banding or HDR clipping problems.
trigger: GUI preview/full render/export display preparation, especially large images, backend materialize_policy='backend', ACES/linear output, or HDR-adjacent preview paths.
recommendation: Separate display preview from export source, support tiled/downscaled display transforms, and preserve at least 16-bit or float through profile conversion when possible. Record when preview is SDR-only.
validation: Benchmark preview memory/time on a 12MP image and add a precision test proving profile conversion does not collapse distinct 16-bit values before display.

title: GPU enlarger LUT mode unconditionally falls back to direct spectral computation and leaves dead LUT code below
evidence: When use_lut is true, _spectral_compute_enlarger_gpu immediately returns _film_cmy_to_print_log_raw(..., return_backend=True) inside a try/finally at printing.py:129-139. The LUT cache/application code at 141-187 is therefore unreachable.
impact: A user can enable LUT settings while GPU execution still performs exact direct spectral work. This is defensible for precision, but it makes performance expectations and code ownership misleading.
recommendation: Either remove/dead-code-gate the unreachable backend LUT branch and document exact direct fallback, or implement a PCHIP-equivalent backend LUT path with CPU parity tests.
validation: Assert timing diagnostics include direct fallback when GPU LUT mode is selected, and add a code-level test that the unreachable branch is intentionally absent or covered.

title: No repository CI workflow is present for a multi-platform HDR/GPU/GUI codebase
evidence: find .github only found .github/FUNDING.yml. Local validation had to run Python, GUI, Halide, Android, and Swift manually. Android ./gradlew test produced no output for more than six minutes and was killed, so there is no automated platform signal for that surface in this review.
impact: Critical contracts such as SDR invariance, HDR metadata, MLX/CPU parity, GUI state wiring, Android JNI, and macOS bridge behavior can regress without any required shared gate.
trigger: Any branch or local dirty worktree changes without a maintained CI matrix.
recommendation: Add a minimal CI matrix: non-GUI pytest, targeted HDR/gain-map tests, lint/static checks, Android unit test or preflight, and Swift package tests where hosted runners support them.
validation: A clean PR should show required green checks for the above suites and publish platform-limited skips explicitly.

title: SimulationWorker catches BaseException and converts fatal interrupts into ordinary failure signals
evidence: SimulationWorker.run catches BaseException at controller_runtime.py:64-69 and emits a failed signal string. BaseException includes KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit, and MemoryError.
impact: Fatal process-level events can be swallowed inside a worker and reported as a normal simulation failure, complicating shutdown and memory-pressure diagnosis.
trigger: Keyboard interrupt, SystemExit, or severe memory error raised in a background simulation request.
recommendation: Catch Exception for normal failures and let BaseException propagate or handle MemoryError/SystemExit explicitly with stronger process-level reporting.
validation: Add unit tests with a fake execute_request raising KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit and assert they are not downgraded to a normal failed signal.

title: RAW EXIF read failures silently disable lens correction context
evidence: _read_exif_metadata catches every Exception at raw_file_processor.py:151-163 and returns empty make/model/lens/focal data. Lens correction later treats missing metadata as no correction.
impact: Damaged or unsupported EXIF can make lens correction silently disappear instead of telling the user that metadata was unavailable.
trigger: RAW/DNG files with unsupported, corrupted, or unreadable EXIF metadata and lens_correction=True.
recommendation: Return structured status or warning text to the GUI/API when EXIF parsing fails. Keep no-op fallback only when the user opted into best-effort correction.
validation: Add a raw processor test where exiv2 raises and assert the returned status exposes the metadata failure.

title: Workspace instructions describe a Linux/no-GUI environment while current validation ran on macOS with GUI tests passing
evidence: The provided AGENTS.md text says 'Linux server (no macOS, no Metal, no GUI display)' and skips GUI/macOS paths, but the current environment is /Users/... on macOS, tests/gui passed with 187 tests, and swift test --package-path macos/SpektrafilmMac passed 10 Swift tests.
impact: Future agents may incorrectly skip macOS/GUI validation or misclassify platform failures because the local instructions do not match the active workstation.
trigger: Any review/fix task that follows AGENTS.md literally in this checkout.
recommendation: Split platform instructions into environment-specific profiles or update AGENTS.md to require live capability detection before skipping macOS/GUI/Metal checks.
validation: Document the current machine capability probe and rerun GUI/macOS smoke after updating instructions.

title: Misspelled highlight utility filename coexists with similarly named highlight code
evidence: Static file inventory includes src/spektrafilm/utils/numba_boost_hightlights.py while searches also show src/spektrafilm/utils/numba_boost_highlights.py. The misspelling increases import/discovery ambiguity.
impact: Minor maintenance friction and higher chance of editing/importing the wrong helper.
trigger: Developers searching for highlight boost utility modules.
recommendation: Keep a compatibility alias if needed, but consolidate on the correctly spelled module name in imports and docs.
validation: rg imports for both spellings and add a deprecation note or alias test if both must remain.

title: Current RouteMaster paper HDR path ignores print density curve morph changes
evidence: The final full-suite validation on the current dirty tree failed tests/test_hdr_routemaster_projection.py::test_paper_mode_responds_to_print_density_curve_morph. The assertion at tests/test_hdr_routemaster_projection.py:102-107 expects changed paper HDR to differ from base after print_render.density_curves_morph.active=True and gamma_factor=1.3 at lines 197-207, but pytest reported the changed and base HDR arrays were allclose. The relevant projection path project_hdr_ideal_paper builds hdr_y from scene_y_raw (src/spektrafilm/hdr/ideal_paper.py:32-42), then _build_result replaces paper pixels at or below diffuse white with legacy SDR and uses route_look_chroma/material detail sidecars (src/spektrafilm/hdr/projection.py:200-213). This proves at least one print-render chemistry control is not reflected in the paper HDR result that the test suite now requires.
impact: Users can alter print chemistry/density curve morph controls and receive an HDR paper export that is numerically unchanged for that control. That breaks the stated paper-HDR semantics and currently makes the non-GUI test suite fail.
trigger: Paper HDR projection/export with print_render.density_curves_morph enabled or changed, especially gamma_factor changes around 1.3 in the current regression test.
recommendation: Trace whether density curve morph should affect route_luminance_y, route_look_chroma, material_detail_y, or the below-white SDR preservation boundary, then wire the paper HDR projection to the intended print-render authority instead of scene_y-only behavior where appropriate. Preserve the light-table invariant that paper controls do not affect film-scan HDR.
validation: Rerun .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_hdr_routemaster_projection.py::test_paper_mode_responds_to_print_density_curve_morph -q, then the HDR slice and full non-GUI suite. Add a focused numeric assertion identifying which RouteMaster sidecar changes when density_curves_morph changes.
